arxiv-2105-08042.title: Dynamics of spectral correlations in the entanglement Hamiltonian of the Aubry-André-Harper model
arxiv-2105-08042.creator: Aamna Ahmed, Nilanjan Roy, Auditya Sharma
arxiv-2105-08042.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Aamna Ahmed, Nilanjan Roy, Auditya Sharma. We numerically study the evolution of spectral correlations in the entanglement Hamiltonian (EH) of non-interacting fermions in the Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) model. We analyze the time evolution of the EH spectrum in a nonequilibrium setting by studying several quantities: spectral distribution, level statistics, entanglement entropy, and spectral form factor (SFF) in the context of the delocalization-localization transition in the AAH model.

arxiv-2201-09860.title: Brownian Motion in the Hilbert Space of Quantum States along with the Ricci Flow and Stochastically Emergent Einstein-Hilbert Action: Formulating a Well-Defined Feynman’s Path-Integral Measure for Quantum Fields in the Presence of Gravity
arxiv-2201-09860.creator: Amir Abbass Varshovi
arxiv-2201-09860.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Amir Abbass Varshovi. Abstract: In this paper, we aim to interpret the background gravitational effects appearing in quantum field theory on curved space-time by studying the Brownian motion of quantum states along with the Hamilton-Perelman Ricci flow. It has been shown that the Wiener measure automatically contains the Einstein-Hilbert action and the path-integral formulation of the scalar quantum field theory on curved space-time at the first order of local approximations.

arxiv-2203-14617.title: Enriching Scholarly Knowledge with Context
arxiv-2203-14617.creator: Muhammad Haris, Markus Stocker, Sören Auer
arxiv-2203-14617.description: Abstract Leveraging a GraphQL-based federated query service that integrates multiple scholarly communication infrastructures (specifically, DataCite, ORCID, ROR, OpenAIRE, Semantic Scholar, Wikidata and Altmetric), we develop a novel web widget based approach for the presentation of scholarly knowledge with rich contextual information.

arxiv-2209-05028.title: Extrema of multinomial assignment process
arxiv-2209-05028.creator: Mikhail Lifshits, Gilles Mordant
arxiv-2209-05028.description: Abstract We study the asymptotic behavior of the expectation of the maxima and minima of random assignment process generated by a large matrix with multinomial entries. A variety of results is obtained for different sparsity regimes. Key words. Expected maxima, minima, multinomial distribution, random assignment process. AMS subject classifications. 60C05 (Primary), 05C70, 60K30 (Secondary). 1 Introduction and main results 1.

arxiv-2209-11555.title: Analysis of Fault Tolerant Multi-stage Switch Architecture for TSN
arxiv-2209-11555.creator: Adnan Ghaderi, Rahul Nandkumar Gore
arxiv-2209-11555.description: Abstract We conducted the feasibility analysis of utilizing a highly available multi-stage architecture for TSN switches used for sending high priority, mission-critical traffic within a bounded latency instead of traditional single-stage architectures. To verify the TSN functionality, we implemented the ’strict priority’ feature.

arxiv-2306-13458.title: Influence Maximization based on Threshold Models in Hypergraphs
arxiv-2306-13458.creator: Renquan Zhang, Xilong Qu, Qiang Zhang, Xirong Xu, Sen Pei*
arxiv-2306-13458.description: Abstract Influence Maximization problem has received significant attention in recent years due to its application in various domains such as product recommendation, public opinion dissemination, and disease propagation. This paper proposes a theoretical analysis framework for collective influence in hypergraphs, focusing on identifying a set of seeds that maximize influence in threshold models.

arxiv-2405-07455.title: New sources of ghost fields in k k -essence theories for black-bounce solutions
arxiv-2405-07455.creator: Carlos F. S. Pereira, Denis C. Rodrigues, Júlio C. Fabris, Manuel E. Rodrigues, Ébano L. Martins
arxiv-2405-07455.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Carlos F. S. Pereira, Denis C. Rodrigues, Júlio C. Fabris, Manuel E. Rodrigues, Ébano L. Martins. In the present study, we generalize the possible ghost field configurations within the framework of k k -essence theory to the Simpson-Visser metric area function Σ 2 = x 2 + a 2 \Sigma^{2}=x^{2}+a^{2} .

arxiv-2503-12616.title: Equivalent-Circuit Thermal Model for Batteries with One-Shot Parameter Identification
arxiv-2503-12616.creator: Myisha A. Chowdhury, Qiugang Lu
arxiv-2503-12616.description: Abstract Accurate state of temperature (SOT) estimation for batteries is crucial for regulating their temperature within a desired range to ensure safe operation and optimal performance. The existing measurement-based methods often generate noisy signals and cannot scale up for large-scale battery packs. The electrochemical model-based methods, on the contrary, offer high accuracy but are computationally expensive.

arxiv-2507-19604.title: On finite β \beta -expansions for the set of natural numbers
arxiv-2507-19604.creator: Túlio O. Carvalho, Catharina M. Moreira
arxiv-2507-19604.description: Abstract We present a study of the problem of finiteness of the β \beta -expansions for the set of natural numbers, condition F 1 F_{1} in brief, for three families of Pisot numbers for which the β \beta -expansion of 1 is not a non-decreasing sequence.

arxiv-2511-21831.title: No need to calibrate: characterization and compilation for high-fidelity circuit execution using imperfect gates
arxiv-2511-21831.creator: Ashish Kakkar, Samuel Marsh, Yulun Wang, Pranav Mundada, Paul Coote, Gavin Hartnett, Michael J. Biercuk, Yuval Baum
arxiv-2511-21831.description: Abstract We propose and validate on real quantum computing hardware a new method for extended two-qubit gate set design, replacing iterative, fine calibration with fast characterization of a small number of gate parameters which are then tracked and corrected in circuit compilation.

arxiv-2512-23456.title: Poles from the conserved kinetic equation : The emerging gradient structure and causality riddle of relativistic hydrodynamics
arxiv-2512-23456.creator: Sukanya Mitra
arxiv-2512-23456.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sukanya Mitra. In this work, the poles and the resulting dispersion spectra from the relativistic kinetic equation have been analyzed with the help of a proposed collision kernel that conserves both the energy-momentum tensor and particle current by construction. The dispersion relations, which originally come out in the form of logarithmic divergences, in the long wavelength limit exhibit the systematic gradient structure of the relativistic hydrodynamics.

europmc-pmc9671812.title: Metabolomic profiles predict individual multidisease outcomes.
europmc-pmc9671812.creator: Buergel T, Steinfeldt J, Ruyoga G, Pietzner M, Bizzarri D, Vojinovic D, Upmeier Zu Belzen J, Loock L, Kittner P, Christmann L, Hollmann N, Strangalies H, Braunger JM, Wild B, Chiesa ST, Spranger J, Klostermann F, van den Akker EB, Trompet S, Mooijaart SP, Sattar N, Jukema JW, Lavrijssen B, Kavousi M, Ghanbari M, Ikram MA, Slagboom E, Kivimaki M, Langenberg C, Deanfield J, Eils R, Landmesser U.

Here we explored the potential of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy-derived metabolomic profiles to inform on multidisease risk beyond conventional clinical...

pmc-10518260.title: Impact of Fixed Combination of Metformin and Pioglitazone on Insulin Resistance of Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: Results of a Randomized Open-Label Study
pmc-10518260.creator: Rui Sun, Lu Yuan, Yun Shen, Ziyang Shen, Bo Ding, Jianhua Ma
pmc-10518260.description: AimTo compare the effect of metformin, a fixed combination of metformin and pioglitazone, or dapagliflozin on insulin resistance in patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes.MethodsIn this 6-week randomized open-label trial, 58 patients were randomly assigned to insulin with metformin, a fixed combination of metformin and pioglitazone, or dapagliflozin for 4 weeks.

pmc-10521273.title: Experience of Autologous Stem Cell Transplant in Multiple Myeloma: The Patient and Caregiver Perspective
pmc-10521273.creator: Doris K Hansen, Todd Bixby, Karen Fixler, Lisa Shea, Christine Brittle, Kimberly Brunisholz, Yi-Hsuan Liu, Jinhai Stephen Huo
pmc-10521273.description: A qualitative study of the experiences of patients who received autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT) for the treatment of multiple myeloma (MM) was conducted to better understand their MM disease journey, including first symptoms, diagnosis, ASCT, and recovery. Sixteen participants, including 12 patients with MM and 4 caregivers of patients with MM, were interviewed in focus group meetings.

pmc-11484713.title: Tumor immune microenvironment analysis of non-small cell lung cancer development through multiplex immunofluorescence
pmc-11484713.creator: Jiaping Zhao, Yu Lu, Zhaofeng Wang, Haiying Wang, Ding Zhang, Jinping Cai, Bei Zhang, Junling Zhang, Mengli Huang, Andreas Pircher, Krishna H Patel, Honggang Ke, Yong Song
pmc-11484713.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundEmerging evidence has underscored the crucial role of infiltrating immune cells in the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) development and progression. With the implementation of screening programs, the incidence of early-stage NSCLC is rising. However, the high risk of recurrence and poor survival rates associated with this disease necessitate a deeper understanding of the TIME and its relationship with driver alterations.

pmc-11564411.title: Olfactory training: perspective from people who were disturbed by their smell problems
pmc-11564411.creator: Zetian Li, Robert Pellegrino, Christine Kelly, Thomas Hummel
pmc-11564411.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeOlfactory training (OT) is an effective and affordable option in the treatment of olfactory dysfunction. Despite significant progress in the field in recent years, some factors influencing OT participation remain unclear.MethodsBased on an anonymous online survey orchestrated by AbScent.org the present study enrolled 450 participants and divided them into OT (n = 161) and No OT (n = 289) groups based on their OT participation.

pmc-12693077.title: Damage Identification in Composite Wind Turbine Blades Using Relative Natural Frequency Changes and Bayesian Probability
pmc-12693077.creator: Panida Kaewniam, Qingyang Wei, Haoan Gu, Nizar Faisal Alkayem, Maosen Cao, Theodore E Matikas
pmc-12693077.description: Structural health monitoring (SHM) of composite wind turbine blades (WTBs) is crucial for improving power efficiency, reducing maintenance costs, and ensuring long-term structural reliability. Traditional frequency-based damage detection, often derived from simplified isotropic beam principles, can be challenged by the anisotropy, heterogeneity, and geometric complexity of composite WTBs.

pmc-13361078.title: GSK3α functions as a stemness checkpoint across multiple stem cell states
pmc-13361078.creator: Duo Wang, Xiukun Wang, Safia Malki, Yanpui Chan, Brian Bennett, Joshua Feng, Jiaqi Tang, Xi Chen, Daniel McKim, Chao Zhang, Litao Tao, Jie Xu, Y. Eugene Chen, Guang Hu, Qi-Long Ying

pmc-13366196.title: Age, Multidomain Lifestyle Intervention, and White Matter Integrity
pmc-13366196.creator: Pauline Maillard, Prashanthi Vemuri, Danielle J. Harvey, Theresa M. Harrison, Ashritha L. Reddy, Hwamee Oh, Stephen Salloway, Simin Mahinrad, Thomas M. Holland, Rachel Whitmer, Mark A. Espeland, Laura D. Baker, Susan M. Landau, Charles DeCarli
pmc-13366196.description: This prespecified secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial assesses whether a multidomain lifestyle intervention, vs a self-guided program, alters trajectories of cerebrovascular magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) markers, whether baseline diffusion MRI estimates subsequent vascular injury, and whether any effects differ by age among adults 60 to 79 years of age who are at increased risk for cognitive decline.

pmc-13495418.title: Ultrasound-assisted deep eutectic solvent extraction of green, high-efficient, and high-bioactive polysaccharides from Glycyrrhiza uralensis
pmc-13495418.creator: Yan Sun, Shandang Shi, Rui Tang, Zhuang Meng, Haitao Shen, Lingling Chen, Fei Wang, Hongbin Li
pmc-13495418.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Graphical abstract Introduction Glycyrrhiza uralensis Fisch., commonly known as licorice, is a perennial herb of the genus Glycyrrhiza within the subfamily Papilionoideae of the family Leguminosae. As among the most widely used herbs in traditional Chinese medicine, G. uralensis displays a broad spectrum of pharmacological benefits, with documented activities including spleen tonification, heat clearance, detoxification, phlegm resolution, cough relief, spasm alleviation, and the modulation of coadministered herbs [1], [2].

pmc-13677193.title: Regulation of spermatozoal capacitation by serotonin
pmc-13677193.creator: Masakatsu FUJINOKI
pmc-13677193.description: Mammalian spermatozoa begin swimming after ejaculation. After spermatozoa enter the oviduct, they undergo capacitation, penetrate the oocyte envelope, and fertilize the oocytes. These processes occur spontaneously but are influenced by hormones and neurotransmitters. Serotonin [5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT)] is a well-known neurotransmitter found in reproductive organs.
